title: category menu — the seven published public-benefit categories
description: THE category vocabulary, published once. The seven public-benefit categories of the association's statutes, Art. 7 (ops decision D33 item 1, confirmed at the founding assembly): health, education, poverty relief, humanitarian aid, environment, animal welfare, research. Nothing anywhere may name a category outside this list — a registry record's `impact_category_defaults`, a manifest's `allocation.defaults`, a ledger row's `category_fund_id` and every public surface resolve against this menu and nothing else, so free text is structurally impossible (ENG-033, D16). A category is the basket of listed recipients assigned to it and nothing else; the recipients themselves are NOT part of this contract — the Recipient List is published separately as the versioned annex to the statutes, which is why `provisional` stays true until that annex exists. `category_id` carries the `cat-*` form the ledger's `category_fund_id` column uses and must equal `cat-{slug}`; JSON Schema cannot express that agreement, so the publishing repository's gate asserts it and so does the curated registry repository's, which vendors this menu byte-identically and checks the bytes against the published copy on every run.

x-psn.artifactPath: (this repository) examples/category-menu.v1.example.json — vendored byte-identically as config/category-funds.json in the curated registry repository
x-psn.producer: the statutes, Art. 7 (steward-published; not derived from any build)
consumers: the curated registry repository's validation CI (FS02-061)

schemaVersion.description: Artifact schema version (FS-00 §6.2). This file is a committed source, not a build product, so it carries no `generatedAt` — there is no build instant to record.

_comment.description: A human note, the way a JSON file carries one. Consumers ignore it. It exists because this file is vendored: the copy a reader finds in another repository must explain, in place, where the canonical copy lives and what keeps the two level.

provisional.description: True while the Recipient List — the named organisations inside each category — is not yet adopted and published as the annex to the statutes. The category NAMES are published either way; `provisional` says nothing about them. A surface that renders a recipient must state that no recipient is listed yet while this is true (honesty rule, FS-00 §6.8).

categories.description: The seven categories, in the order Art. 7 lists them. Exactly seven: the count is constitutional, not a configuration bound, and a menu of six or eight is a defect rather than a variation. `uniqueItems` rejects a duplicated ROW; a duplicated slug across two differing rows is caught by the gates, which assert this list against the published slug set.

slug.description: The stable machine token. It is what a registry record and a manifest name, so it never changes: a renamed slug would silently invalidate every record that used the old one.

category_id.description: The ledger's identifier for the same category (`category_fund_id`), always `cat-{slug}`. Two spellings exist because the money side was named before the menu was; they are asserted equal rather than assumed.

name.description: The published display name. Public copy: it appears on the allocation surfaces verbatim, so it is not a place for a synonym.

slug.description: The closed slug set, alphabetical here so a diff of the enum is readable; the published ORDER is the one `categories` carries. Every other contract in this set that accepts a category slug carries a copy of this enum, because a published schema must validate on its own download (no external `$ref`); the publishing repository's gate asserts every copy is identical.

categoryId.description: The same seven, in the ledger's `cat-*` spelling.
